_comment: NETWORKS WHOSE UPSTREAM IS GONE, so a repairable refusal on them is no longer repairable.
THIS IS NOT A CHANGE TO `refusal-reasons.json`, AND IT MUST NOT BECOME ONE. That file
classifies each MEMBER `permanent` or `repairable`, once, for every chain — and those
classifications are still right. `not-attempted` really does mean the run stopped rather
than the chain refusing, and on a chain whose network is still up, re-running the range
still produces the trace. Sui's `runtime-refused` rows are the live example: a Sui build
with trace hooks in pre-38 layers would trace them, so they are repairable and must keep
saying so.
What this file carries is the OTHER half of the claim, which no member can carry: whether
the network that would serve the repair still exists. Durability is a property of the
PAIR (member, chain), and splitting it this way is what keeps one chain's obituary from
rewording another chain's rows.
A CHAIN LISTED HERE DOES NOT LOSE ITS PUBLISHED REASONS. Every row keeps the member and
the sentence the producer wrote, because both were TRUE WHEN WRITTEN — the repair really
was available then. What changes is only the durability the page infers from them, which
is the one claim that silently went stale when the network went away.
EVIDENCE IS REQUIRED AND IS A MEASUREMENT, not a press release. The test is not whether
the endpoint answers — a restarted rollup answers perfectly well, at its own low block
numbers, and a request for a LOW height even returns a plausible header belonging to a
different chain. The test is whether the endpoint still serves a height inside the range
we captured.

networks.evidence: https://aztec.drpc.org answers, and is at tip 3,403 against our captured head of 102,690. node_getBlock at any height inside the captured range returns `Unknown block` (code 26). The capture recorded l1ChainId 1 and nodeVersion 5.2.0.
networks.note: Aztec mainnet was restarted after this history was captured. The network that served it no longer exists, so no transaction here can be re-executed, whatever an individual row's published reason says about what that run did or did not try.

networks.evidence: https://aztec-testnet.drpc.org answers, and is at tip 9,405 against our captured head of 99,092. node_getBlock at 45,000, 75,800 and 99,091 — heights this corpus covers, two of them inside ranges that were successfully replayed in September — returns `Unknown block` (code 26). The node now reports nodeVersion 6.0.0, l1ChainId 11155111 and rollupVersion 679261766.
